transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, doctor. I'm here because I've been feeling extremely depressed and sad for about a month now. It just feels like a constant, heavy cloud of gloom that I can't seem to shake off.

In your life, have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or euphoric, to the point where you didn't need much sleep and felt like you could accomplish anything?

Yes, absolutely, I've experienced times exactly like that, and it actually lasted for about six months. During that period, my mood was incredibly elevated and euphoric, and I felt this constant overflow of physical and mental energy. I barely slept at all because I didn't feel the need to, yet I'd wake up feeling completely refreshed and ready to take on multiple activities.

During those six months of high energy, did you ever experience things that others couldn't see or hear, or hold beliefs that seemed clearly untrue to other people, even when you were not feeling depressed?
No, I never experienced anything like that during those months. I didn't see or hear things that others couldn't, and I never held any beliefs that other people found untrue.
During that six-month period of high energy, did your behavior become so intense that it caused significant problems in your work or social life, or did it require you to be hospitalized?

I'm not really sure if it caused major problems for others, but it definitely didn't lead to anything as extreme as being hospitalized. I mostly just felt like I was super productive, even if I was a bit scattered.
Did your friends, family, or colleagues notice a distinct change in your behavior or express concern that you were acting differently than your usual self during that time?
To be honest, I'm not really sure if they noticed. I haven't really asked any of them about it, and no one came up to me directly to say anything at the time.

Since you mentioned this high-energy period lasted for six months, was there any point during that time where your energy or mood was so intense that it was clearly noticeable to others as a change from your baseline, even if they didn't voice concern?

Looking back, my behavior during those six months must have been highly noticeable to others because it was a drastic departure from my normal self. I was constantly on the go, rapidly shifting between extreme moods, and starting multiple projects at once that I never actually finished. I was also going on reckless spending sprees, which is something I would never normally do.

Did these reckless spending sprees or the rapid shifting of projects cause you to experience significant financial difficulty, or did they result in trouble at your workplace or with your personal relationships?

Yes, the reckless spending sprees absolutely caused severe financial distress for both me and my family, leaving us with a lot of debt. I was also starting multiple projects and abandoning them halfway through, which made my daily life feel incredibly chaotic. But without a doubt, the financial strain from my shopping was the most concrete and damaging problem.
